title: Same Keys. Different Tables. Different Speed.

data.kicker: Computer science cheat sheet · 6 collision strategies
title: Same Keys.
Different Tables.
Different Speed.

intro.before: Sooner or later two keys hash to the same slot. How the table handles it sets
intro.highlight: memory, cache hits and worst cases

bullets.text: Colliding keys share one linked list; a delete is a plain unlink
Expected list length is the load factor α = n/m: O(1 + α) per lookup
Java HashMap turns a bucket into a tree once it passes 8 entries
Every entry is its own node: extra pointers and a cache miss per hop
On a collision, try slot h+1, h+2, … until an empty one turns up
Probes read neighbouring slots, so most land in the same cache line
At load 0.5 a hit takes 1.5 probes on average, a miss 2.5 (Knuth)
Runs merge into clusters: at load 0.9 a miss averages 50.5 probes
Offsets 0, 1, 3, 6, 10…: each jump is one longer, escaping crowded runs
In a power-of-2 table, these triangular offsets visit every slot once
Abseil and Rust's hashbrown jump between 16-slot groups (x86) this way
Keys with the same home follow the same path: secondary clustering
A second hash sets each key's step: probe h1(k) + i·h2(k)
Keys 14 and 21 share home 0 but step by 5 and 2: no shared path
At load 0.9 a miss averages about 10 probes, vs 50.5 for linear
Each probe jumps far (a likely cache miss); step must be coprime to m
Linear probing where a key far from home evicts one nearer its home
Evens out probe lengths: here the worst drops from 4 slots to 2
A miss stops early, at the first key closer to home than itself
Inserts swap and shift keys, so writes cost more than plain probing
Every key has exactly two possible slots, one per hash function
A lookup checks at most 2 slots: O(1) in the worst case, not on average
Multi-slot buckets let DPDK's rte_hash fill more than 90% of slots
1-slot tables must stay under 50% full; eviction loops force a rehash

online.note: h(k) mod m picks a home slot

online.note: chain node, +1, growing jump or h2(k) step

online.name: Move other keys
online.note: swap or evict to keep lookups short

principles.lead: The load factor sets the speed.
principles.sub: Java HashMap grows at 0.75 full; Abseil's Swiss tables grow at 7/8.

principles.lead: A weak hash breaks every scheme.
principles.sub: With h(k) = k mod 8, keys 8, 16, 24 and 32 all land in slot 0.
Hit/miss ratio, key size and delete rate pick the winner, not textbook averages.

quote.big: Collisions are certain. Slow lookups aren't.
quote.small: Same keys, different strategy, different speed.
